title: Self-hosted applications with free OIDC login
notes: These projects can be self-hosted and provide basic OIDC/OAuth2 login without buying an SSO add-on.
You still need an OIDC identity provider, such as Keycloak, authentik, or Zitadel.
Hosting, support, advanced provisioning, and group-sync features may have separate commercial offerings. Verify the feature against the version you deploy.
Outline is included because its free self-hosted edition includes OIDC, but its current BSL-1.1 license is not OSI-approved open source.

applications.name: BookStack
applications.description: A self-hosted documentation and wiki platform with built-in OpenID Connect authentication, user matching, and optional group sync.

applications.name: Gitea
applications.description: A lightweight self-hosted Git service that can authenticate users through OAuth2/OIDC providers, including generic providers.

applications.name: GitLab Self-Managed
applications.license: MIT (Community Edition) / GitLab Enterprise Edition license
applications.oidc_support: Available in the Free self-managed tier

applications.name: Forgejo
